fields.meta_description: Build a class registration form that caps every section and bills tuition by the term or month, with each student saved to a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Class Registration Form for Every Section and Term
fields.hero_description: Describe your class schedule, the seats in each section and how tuition works. Emergent builds the class registration form, fills sections in order and keeps every student on file.
fields.features_heading: What Runs Behind Each Class Sign-Up
fields.features_subheading: Six jobs a front desk would otherwise handle with a clipboard and a spreadsheet.
fields.feature_1:
Sections that fill to their own limit

Add each section of a class with its meeting time and a seat limit. A full section closes, and the form offers the next section of the same class that still has a seat open.
fields.feature_2:
Classes matched to age or level

Set the age range or skill level each class serves. A parent enters a birth date or picks the last level passed, and the form lists only the classes that student can join this term.
fields.feature_3:
Term dates with closures removed

Enter the first and last class of the term, then each date the studio is closed. Every section counts the weeks it meets, and tuition and attendance sheets follow that count.
fields.feature_4:
Tuition by the term or the month

Connect Stripe to collect a full term at sign-up or to bill monthly tuition to a saved card. Each student's row shows what has been paid so far and the date of the next payment.
fields.feature_5:
Makeup classes with a limit per term

Let a student who misses class book another section that has an open seat. The form counts each makeup against the limit you set and adds the student to that section's roster.
fields.feature_6:
The whole app exported to GitHub

Send the full registration app to GitHub on paid plans when a developer wants to add attendance tracking or a teacher payroll report. It can also run on your studio's own domain.
fields.why_title: Why Build Class Registration With Emergent?
fields.why_description: A PDF signs up one student for one class. It cannot see that Tuesday is full or bill the second month of tuition.

fields.usecase_heading: Registration for Four Kinds of Classes
fields.tab_content_1:
Twelve seats each on Tuesday and Thursday

Brightwater Dance runs Ballet 1 for ages 6 to 8 in two sections, each capped at 12 dancers. Tuesday at 4:30 is full. When a parent registers a 7-year-old, the form hides Tuesday and offers Thursday at 4:30, which has 3 seats left. The front desk sees both rosters side by side.
fields.tab_content_2:
Joining in week 4 costs $100 for 5 lessons

Saturday lessons at Lakeview Swim School run as an 8-week session for $160, which works out to $20 a lesson. A parent who signs up in week 4 sees the 5 lessons that remain and pays $100 at checkout. The child goes onto the Level 2 roster from that Saturday on.
fields.tab_content_3:
One saved card, $140 on the 1st of every month

Harbor Music School bills piano students by the month. A parent booking weekly 30-minute lessons enters a card once, and the form starts a $140 monthly subscription in Stripe that bills on the 1st. The student's row shows the lesson slot and the next charge date.
fields.tab_content_4:
Makeups booked into any section with a free mat

Each yoga term at Elm Street Community Ed runs 10 weeks and allows 2 makeup classes. Dana Reyes misses Monday's 6 PM class and picks from the sections with an open mat. Wednesday at 6 PM has 2, and booking it adds her to that roster and marks 1 of 2 makeups used.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Class Registration Form
fields.howto_description: Most of the work is deciding how sections fill and how tuition is charged.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write out the term calendar first
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Give every section its own seat count
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set the age or level for each class
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the opening and closing dates of the term and every date you are closed. Note whether students can join after the term starts, and if they can, whether the price drops for the weeks they missed or stays the same.
fields.howto_step_2_des: A class may meet several times a week. Write each section as its own line with a weekday, a start time and a seat limit. Then say which section the form should offer when a family's first choice is full.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide what places a student in a class: a birth date, the last level passed or a teacher's note. Write down the range each class accepts. Families will then see only the classes their child qualifies for this term.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick one payment per term or a monthly charge on a saved card. Stripe handles both once it is connected. Then decide what the form charges a student who starts partway through, whether a share of the term or the full price.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the calendar, the sections and the tuition rules into one prompt, then add the questions you ask each family. Emergent builds the form, the payment step and a database of students and sections. Ask for changes the same way.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Put the makeup policy in writing
fields.howto_step_6_des: State how many makeups a student gets per term and whether a makeup can be taken in a different level. The form needs both answers to show the right open seats when someone misses a week.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Sign up a test student for a section that is already full and pay with a Stripe test card. Check that a full section points the family to another one and that the charge is right. Delete the test record before families get the link.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is two Jotform template pages and six PDFs: a dance studio's new-student sheet, an LA recreation center's activity form, a university advising form and three government course sign-ups. Each records one student for one class on one date. A studio, swim school or community-ed program that runs classes week after week needs what a sheet cannot hold: several sections of the same class with their own seat counts, a session that a child can join halfway through, tuition that recurs every month, and makeup classes when someone misses a week. This page shows four programs running recurring classes that way and answers the template, PDF, Word and registration-versus-enrollment questions plainly. One-off workshops stay on the workshop sibling; grade placement and school enrollment stay on the student sibling.
